seed_draft: Shelah's independence property is a combinatorial dividing line for formulas in model theory. Vapnik and Chervonenkis introduced classes of sets of finite VC dimension in probability and learning theory. We show that a formula is without the independence property exactly when the family of sets it defines has finite VC dimension. This lets results about VC classes (such as uniform convergence of empirical measures) be applied to definable sets, and conversely. We give examples from o-minimal and stable theories.
notes: Evidence is snippet-level; fetch the NIP guide before relying on it. Seed from general knowledge; last two sentences are a guess at content. Equivalence itself is nearly definitional, so Type 4 (three new statements) is the live bar.

seed_draft: Let H be an n x n matrix all of whose entries are complex numbers z with z^l = 1, and suppose H times its conjugate transpose equals n times the identity. Which pairs (n,l) admit such an H? Factor l as a product of s distinct prime powers q_1^{e_1}...q_s^{e_s}. We study the necessary condition that n can be written as c_1 q_1 + ... + c_s q_s with all c_j non-negative integers. When s=1 this reduces to a standard divisibility fact. We establish it for s=2 and s=3, and conjecture it for every s. We end with remarks on other obstructions known for such matrices.
notes: Same claim as N1 (s=2,3 proved, s>=4 conjectured) with unitary-matrix wording, q_j for prime powers, c_j coefficients. Avoid the words Hadamard/roots-of-unity in the title when running. Check a web search on a seed sentence before use.

seed_draft: Fix an integer k>=3 and coefficients a_1..a_k, b with a_1+...+a_k not zero, so that the equation a_1x_1+...+a_kx_k=b is not preserved under shifting all variables. Call a subset of {1,...,N} free if it contains no solution. The largest free sets are known; we ask how many free sets there are in total, conjecturing that the count is 2^{(1+o(1)) m} where m is the maximum size. We prove a weakened version for a family of such equations by associating to each equation a nearly regular graph on {1,...,N} whose independent sets are exactly the free sets, and counting those independent sets. This extends to general equations the known counting question for sum-free sets.

seed_draft: Let C be a finite collection of convex bodies in d-dimensional space such that no m+1 of them are pairwise disjoint. We ask for the smallest number of hyperplanes, each perpendicular to a coordinate axis, such that every body in C is cut by at least one of them. We prove that this smallest number is bounded by a function f(d,m) alone. First bound is super-exponential, then a polynomial bound in m for fixed d. In the plane we lower the best exponential bound to O(m^2).

seed_draft: Association schemes admit a construction in which one scheme is placed on top of another, so that the relations of the second refine one class of the first. We define a counterpart of this construction for table algebras. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition for a table algebra to decompose as such a composite of two smaller ones. Moreover, if the dual objects of two commutative table algebras are again table algebras, then the dual of their composite is a table algebra, isomorphic to the composite of the duals taken in the opposite order. Consequences for association schemes follow.
notes: Same claim as N4. "Wedge product" replaced by "composite where one scheme refines a class of the other" (the actual wedge product is what is meant; check the definition against the original before use). Verify that the original's claimed owner theorem (Blau 2013) still applies.
